g.text: After the 202 the client does not wait on the queue:
it polls GET /dubbing/:id (or listens via SSE / WebSocket)
and reads status + progress from the database.
stalled (worker died / lock lost) → back to wait
BullMQ rules that matter for Dubbio
• Job payload = IDs only (dubbingId). Videos and audio live in R2, never in Redis.
• Retries are job options: attempts + backoff. failed → delayed → wait, and the processor restarts at step 1.
• processor returns → BullMQ moves the job to completed. processor throws → failed. Nothing to "mark" by hand.
• Long jobs (minutes): keep the event loop free. A lost lock = stalled → the job runs again (lockDuration, maxStalledCount).
• Call job.updateProgress(n) after every step so the UI can show progress.
• Final failure (attempts exhausted): set DB status = FAILED in the worker "failed" event.
• Concurrency = how many jobs one worker runs at once. Scale with more worker processes.
ONE job = the whole pipeline. A retry restarts at step 1 and pays ElevenLabs / TwelveLabs again.
Local tool on the worker: ffmpeg / Demucs
